entry.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis. Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world.
entry.summary:
Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs).

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics #agents

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
entry.summary:
We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #optimization #post-quantum

entry.title: Painlevé representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
entry.summary:

We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. entry.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
entry.summary:
An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #decision-theory #algebra-geometry

entry.title: Graphs and cycles in curve-based collision walks. In this work, we look at collision-based attacks both for elliptic curve and isogeny problems.
entry.summary:
In this work, we look at collision-based attacks both for elliptic curve and isogeny problems. Our main focus is on attacks in the multi-user setting, i.e., where one tries to recover all secret keys of a large set of $L$ public keys simultaneously, in a faster way than the total time required to attack each key individually. We consider three different problems: (1) the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves, (2) the isogeny pathfinding problem on supersingular $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$-curves, (3) the isogeny pathfinding problem on supersingular $\mathbb{F}_p$-curves.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: A New Approach to Reducing Modulus Requirements in Homomorphic Computation: Precision Allocation in CKKS
entry.summary:
Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation over encrypted data subject to the prescribed security and precision requirements (allowable deviations from ideal results). Among all FHE schemes, CKKS is a representative scheme for approximate arithmetic, allowing the same operation on multiple values packed into a single RLWE ciphertext. Reducing ciphertext modulus $Q$ for given output precision requirements under RLWE security constraints is a central challenge in homomorphic computation.

entry.title: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03443-9 The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

entry.title: Computing the Nucleon of Matching Games
entry.summary:
The nucleon is the multiplicative counterpart of the nucleolus: it lexicographically maximizes the fraction of its stand-alone value that each coalition receives. We study exact nucleon computation in matching games and in two extensions: $b$-matching games, in which players may have several partners, and partitioned matching games, in which one player may own several vertices. We resolve three open problems from a recent survey.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #combinatorics

entry.title: Urban climate regressions require representative monitoring networks
entry.summary:
Land use regression models relate intra-urban air temperature to spatial predictors such as building volume, tree canopy cover and topography, and are increasingly used to produce fine-scale temperature maps. However, the accuracy of these estimates can be compromised by unrepresentative monitoring networks. Here we show that reference weather station networks, designed for regional rather than intra-urban monitoring, sample only a narrow portion of a city's spatial heterogeneity, missing both the densely built core and the cool, vegetated periphery that set the two ends of the urban temperature range.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #climate-earth #combinatorics
